marten [ḥulda] and … pit. … And if this … who believes in … a pit and a marten, … all the more so

marten [ḥulda] and the pit. Once a young man saved a girl who had fallen into a pit. After rescuing her they swore to remain faithful to each other, and they declared the pit and a passing marten their witnesses. As time went by the young man forgot his vow and married another woman. They had two children, both of whom died tragically, one by falling into a pit and the other when he was bitten by a marten. Their unusual deaths led the young man to realize his error and he returned to the first woman. And if this is the outcome for one who believes in signs from a pit and a marten, all the more so
one who has faith in the Holy One, … Blessed be He.
one who has faith in the Holy One, Blessed be He.
